questions.q: What is a Salesforce "application," per this lesson?
options: A curated container of tabs, branding, and visibility settings built on top of the existing platform — not separate installed software
A standalone piece of software installed outside of Salesforce
A synonym for a single custom object
A type of report that only administrators can run
questions.explain: An app is configuration — tabs, branding, nav order, and visibility — not a separately installed codebase.

questions.q: Where does a user go to open any app they have access to?
questions.explain: The App Launcher (the grid icon) is where every app a user can open is listed, standard and custom alike.

questions.q: Which Setup page lists every app that exists in an org, standard and custom?
questions.explain: App Manager (Setup → Quick Find → "App Manager") is the admin's master inventory of every app, including the "New Lightning App" button.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things an app bundles together, per this lesson?
questions.explain: An app bundles tabs, branding, navigation order, and profile visibility — no Apex trigger is required to build one.

questions.q: What is the visual/technical difference between a standard Salesforce app (like Sales) and a custom-built app, once the custom app exists?
options: There is no meaningful difference — both appear the same way in the App Launcher
Custom apps cannot have a home page
Custom apps cannot be assigned to user profiles
questions.explain: Once built, a custom app looks and behaves like a standard one in the App Launcher — there's no technical distinction a user would notice.
